items.prompt: A library adds a private Impl field. Public signatures and supported GCC/libstdc++ ABI settings are unchanged. The original client.o hash stays the same, while quote.cpp is recompiled and the executable relinked and run. What has this experiment established?

options.text: Private implementation change and unchanged-client relink worked for this tested ABI/toolchain.
options.why: The measured boundary is local. It demonstrates a useful PIMPL property without asserting compatibility across arbitrary ABIs.

options.text: Any later compiler and standard-library version must accept the original client object.
options.why: The experiment held those ABI conditions fixed; it cannot justify arbitrary toolchain changes.

options.text: Quote has the size of one raw pointer on every target.
options.why: A successful relink does not prove a representation identity, and unique_ptr layout is implementation-dependent.

options.text: Every Quote method is faster because client.o did not change.
options.why: Object reuse is not a timing measurement and says nothing by itself about allocation, indirection or inlining cost.

items.explanation: The measured boundary is local. It demonstrates a useful PIMPL property without asserting compatibility across arbitrary ABIs.
